A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOND/iP-VAE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction, sparsity, classification, convergence, and OOD experiments in Figures 3–4, Table 2, and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds latent-capacity, runtime, color-image, and sample-generation results.

M1.justification: The core FOND inference and training procedures remain. Appendix C.10 adds an iterative generation procedure, Algorithm 1, which feeds decoded images back into inference and repeatedly resamples latent variables.

E1.justification: Appendix C.9 adds training and evaluation on CelebA at 128×128 and RGB CIFAR-10/Tiny ImageNet at 32×32. V2 already used cropped grayscale ImageNet images for OOD testing, so the color-image training coverage is the relevant extension. C.10 also adds MNIST sample generation as a task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the amortized VAEs, PC, iPC, LCA, hierarchical/single-level ia-VAE, and sa-VAE. The added color-image comparison reuses P-VAE counterparts. Newly discussed BONG and reasoning models are not added empirical baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include a K=32–2048 sweep at Ttrain=16 and beta=24, runtime measurements at batch sizes 1 and 10,000, spatial latent configurations for color images, and 100-iteration generation displays. These are added evaluation designs; retained MNIST/OOD settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds controlled latent-capacity sensitivity analysis (C.5), runtime-versus-performance analysis (C.7), and a CelebA comparison crossing inference type with linear/deep decoders (C.9). Existing MAP-decoding, beta/training-depth, rotation, and cross-domain analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new checklist specifies boxplot summaries and a t-distribution assumption for confidence intervals. V2 already reported 99% intervals from five random initializations in Table 2, retained as v3 Table 3; no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: Figures 4 and 9 revise plotted trade-off points and boxplots, including LCA and iGrelu-VAE. New capacity, runtime, color-image, and generation results are added; for example, Table 4 reports CelebA deep iP-VAE R²=0.95 and sparsity=0.93. The original MNIST table values and OOD plots are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B.7.5 corrects the nonlinear Gaussian-phi dynamics: v2 Equation (49) evaluates the decoder Jacobian at z, whereas v3 Equation (48) evaluates it at phi(z). This corrects the chain-rule expression. Most other mathematical differences are equivalent notation, renumbering, or relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explicit claim of scalability to complex color-image datasets. The central claims about deriving spiking inference through FOND, reconstruction–sparsity benefits, and OOD generalization remain, as does the conclusion's central message.

C2.justification: D.5.1 changes the computational limitation from substantial training and inference costs to manageable inference costs with longer training. New interpretations connect increasing capacity to a stable activity budget, iterative computation to serial scaling, and generation class imbalance to the learned prior.

D1.justification: V3 supplies CUDA-event timing code and additional architecture, latent-shape, kernel-size, hyperparameter, and generation settings for its new studies. Existing implementation documentation and the stated code/data/checkpoint access remain.

R1.justification: Appendix D.1 substantially expands FOND's positioning relative to BLR and BONG, contrasting inference-variable dynamics with parameter learning and Monte Carlo differentiation with Gaussian analytical gradients. Additional discussion connects the work to looped transformers, recurrent reasoning models, and the serial scaling hypothesis.

P1.justification: V3 reorganizes the central exposition around a dedicated FOND Section 3 before the Poisson derivation, rewrites the abstract and substantial positioning/cost discussion, and swaps Appendices B.1/B.2. It also adds a paper checklist. These changes substantially reshape the narrative while retaining most derivations.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 2, 4, and 5, the six-panel runtime Figure 12, generation trajectories/sample grids in Figure 18, and Algorithm 1. Retained OOD figures are resized and repositioned. These are substantial display additions beyond pagination and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 already contains the central derivations and extensive reconstruction/OOD evidence. V3 improves exposition, corrects the nonlinear Jacobian, and strengthens practical support through capacity, runtime, and color-image evaluations. The net gain is limited by new reporting inconsistencies: C.7 gives approximately 400/2000 ms convergence times, whereas Figure 12's caption states 200–300 ms.
